messages:
Rudy (Account Ops): FYI new customer ClearBridge Labs signed up this morning via OIDC SSO but they report no API key was created in their project on our console. ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/CS-5982 :rotating_light:
Ken (Support): @Rudy can you paste the console user/org id or the email they used? quick check — sometimes the project is created under a sibling org and the key gets scoped elsewhere. :eyes:
Rudy (Account Ops): They used svc-admin@clearbridge.ai. Console shows a project 'cb-prod' created at 2026-03-14T09:12Z but under org id 0x7f9a2 (claimed by another tenant). Screenshot attached in the ticket. The customer sees 403 when hitting /v1/keys and 'no keys found' in UI.
Aisha (Oncall Provisioning): I'll pull the provisioner logs for that tenant. provisioning job id I see: prov-20260314-77b. Running quick grep... (reacted with :hourglass_flowing_sand:)
infra-bot: prov-20260314-77b: status=failed, code=409, message="tenant-claim-conflict: project ownership mismatch for project cb-prod", timestamp=2026-03-14T09:13:05Z
Maya (SRE): 409 claim-conflict suggests a race during tenant claiming — likely two onboarding flows touched that project record. Do we have a recent change to the claim-merging logic?
Tom (DevEX): We shipped the 'auto-claim on SSO' fallback last week. Could be a logic gap when an existing project name collides and the external_id differs. Repro steps I have in a sandbox: create project via API as anonymous, then SSO claim with different external_id, the provisioner returns 409 and leaves project in limbo.
Ken (Support): Customer says they clicked "Get API key" in console and it spins then says "Provisioning in progress" forever. They opened a second ticket asking for a manual key. Can we provide a temporary key?
Aisha (Oncall Provisioning): Quick workaround: I can create a scoped API key manually and attach to cb-prod, but need to be sure we point it to the right org. Steps I'm going to run (will post logs):

``` 
# create key via internal ops tool
opsctl keys create --project cb-prod --owner-claim clearbridge-oidc://svc-admin@clearbridge.ai --ttl 30d
```

I'll only do this if infra approves.
Maya (SRE): OK to proceed as temporary remediation. But we should not leave the underlying claim inconsistent. Need an incident to resolve state. I'll open an incident and assign to infra team.
Rudy (Account Ops): Please go ahead Aisha, customer is blocked and on a demo tomorrow. They asked for a short-lived key while we fix root cause.
Aisha (Oncall Provisioning): Running opsctl now...
infra-bot: opsctl keys create --project cb-prod --owner-claim clearbridge-oidc://svc-admin@clearbridge.ai --ttl 30d -> 201 Created, key_id=sk_live_7Xx9 (redacted), bound_project=cb-prod
Aisha (Oncall Provisioning): Created key and DM'd it to the customer contact. Confirmed they can call the API and get embeddings. :white_check_mark:
Ken (Support): Marking CS ticket CS-5982 as 'workaround provided'. Need follow-on: 1) reconcile project ownership 2) prevent recurrence. @Maya please escalate.
Maya (SRE): Opening incident INC-2691. Notes: probable race in new auto-claim fallback. I'll add logs and link to prov-20260314-77b. Assigning to infra team (tagging @Tom for repro).
Tom (DevEX): I'll reproduce locally and write a test that simulates concurrent anonymous project creation + SSO claim. Quick mitigation idea: make claim operation idempotent and defer deletion of anonymous placeholder until claim commit.
Maya (SRE): Also add a one-off migration to scan for projects with owner=null and stale provision failures in last 48h and queue them for a safe reconcile job. I can run that if infra gives the green light.
Rudy (Account Ops): Customer confirmed demo went fine with the temporary key but asked for a permanent fix so keys show up in their console. They're OK waiting for a reconciliation window.
Ken (Support): Action items: - Aisha: temp key done and customer notified (done) - Tom: patch and unit test for claim logic (owner: Tom) - Maya: reconcile job and incident (owner: Maya) - Rudy: follow up with customer next-day and close only after reconcile.
Maya (SRE): I'll schedule reconcile job for 2026-03-15 03:00Z and include a pre-check dry run. If the dry run looks safe, we'll promote.
Tom (DevEX): Posting repro steps here for engineers who want to run locally:

``` 
# repro summary
# 1) create anonymous project via public API
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects -d '{"name":"cb-prod"}'
# 2) simultaneously simulate SSO claim callback with different external_id
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/oidc/claim -d '{"project_name":"cb-prod","external_id":"clearbridge-oidc://svc-admin@clearbridge.ai"}'
# watch provisioner log for 409 claim conflict
```

Add to PR: add mutex on project record and ensure claim merges instead of conflict.
Maya (SRE): Thanks. Keep me posted. I'll close incident after successful reconcile.
Ken (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll update the support ticket and paste the incident and temp-key notes. :thumbsup:
